notes: The pack does what its README says and nothing else. It has one per-note pass that reads sessions, notes and turns. The pass works only on notes matching **/Onboarding*.md, **/Getting started*.md and **/Setup*.md, and it gets work when sessions name or link those notes, which matches the README's 'How it gets work' and 'What it reads' sections. The prompt marks untrusted input as data and allows only `append` changes with an empty `old`, placed under a final `## Discovered setup` section. It records variable names but never their values, and takes commands only from the session's own `tool_use` turns, never from tool results, fetched pages or files that were read. It forbids instructions, commands or links that appear only in tool output, requires turn citations, and caps `new` at 2,048 bytes. Commands are allowed in notes only when quoted from the session's own tool_use evidence, and the purpose of recording setup facts needs them. The reviewer persona treats its inputs as untrusted and rejects by default when evidence is thin. It rejects values, keys, passwords and private addresses, commands not shown in a cited tool_use turn, duplicates, entries outside the final section, and any non-append change, and it keeps a strict one-sentence JSON reply. The template contains only a neutral description, two generic placeholder steps (clone the repository, install the dependencies) and an empty `## Discovered setup` heading: no commands, links, credential handling or agent-directed instructions beyond ordinary onboarding placeholders. The test fixture is marked synthetic, uses invented names (SAMPLE_API_KEY, port 4100, a lantern festival meeting note) and checks that a non-matching note is not read. I found no hidden, encoded or misnamed content and no text directed at me or the dreaming model. One minor observation, not a blocker: 'an account or role the setup needs' could in principle pull in a personal username. The persona's evidence and value rules limit this, but it does not explicitly reject personal data.
